concept: Programs break: a bug is a mistake in a program
alt: The Debug Lab opens a program that does not work: Bolt waits at the start while the broken program fills the tray.

concept: Expected and actual: compare what Bolt did with what you expected
alt: Bolt has run part of the broken program and stopped in the wrong place: what Bolt did is not what the program promised.

concept: Step, stop, fix: step one block at a time and stop at the first surprise
alt: Stepping one block at a time: the first block is lit in the tray and Bolt has moved exactly one square.

concept: One too many: a repeat count one too big is a common bug
alt: The broken program is one repeat block set to 6, but the flag is five squares away: one move too many.

actions.program: move; move; move; right; move; move; move

concept: Done means tested: a fix is done when you run it again
alt: The fixed program sits in the tray: the wrong turn left has become turn right, ready to run again and be tested.

concept: Expect bugs: a test case is one board with a known right answer
alt: A Pro Debug Lab board with its test tabs above it: one program must pass every board, not just this one.

actions.program: repeat 5 { move }; left; repeat until goal { move }

concept: One board can hide a bug: the same program on a second test board
alt: The same program on Test 3, a longer hallway: Test 1 and Test 2 show a check, Test 3 a cross, and Bolt splashed into the water.

concept: Edge cases: unusual boards break quiet assumptions
alt: A later Debug Lab board with an unusual layout: goals and walls sit where a program that assumes too much will fail.

actions.program: repeat 5 { move }; left; repeat until goal { move }

concept: The debug loop: a fix is done only when every test passes
alt: After a run, every test tab shows a mark: Test 1 and Test 2 pass, Test 3 fails, so this fix is not done yet.

concept: Meet Pim: every message must reach the right house
alt: Pim opens the Netville map: houses, roads and the first message waiting to be delivered.

concept: Too big to send: the network cuts a message into numbered packets
alt: Break It Up: a message too big for one trip is cut into small numbered packets at the post office.

concept: Back in order: numbers put arriving packets back together
alt: Packets are on the roads of Netville, each carrying its number, so the far end can rebuild the message in order.

concept: Many roads: each packet can take a different road through routers
alt: Many Roads: the town map offers more than one road between the same houses, and a closed road is not the end.

concept: Lock it up: lock it, keep the key, keep a spare copy
alt: The mailbox key builder: pick words for a passphrase, the key that locks your mailbox in Packet Post.

concept: Private or fine to share? Some things stay private
alt: The sharing sort: cards to split into Share and Keep Private, from favorite animals to passphrases.

concept: Build a passphrase: four random words, long and hard to guess
alt: The passphrase is taking shape: words are being picked for the mailbox key, and longer means harder to guess.

concept: Who may know it? Only a trusted adult may know your passphrase
alt: Okay to Tell: a sorting round about who may hear what, where a passphrase is never fine to share.

concept: Keep a spare copy: a backup kept somewhere else
alt: A Good Spare Copy: the sorting round that tells a real backup, kept somewhere else, from a copy that is not.

concept: Secret codes for fun: a cipher wheel shifts each letter by the key (shift 3)
alt: The cipher wheel: turn the key and every letter shifts, turning a plain message into a secret one.

concept: Messages in packets: numbered, routed and rebuilt at the other end
alt: Rules of the Road opens: numbered packets wait at the first router, ready to travel by the shared rules.

concept: Rules everyone follows: a protocol is rules every computer agrees on
alt: A second protocol level: every router on the road follows the same rules, or no packet could be passed on.

concept: Say got it: the receiver confirms each packet and asks for missing ones
alt: The delivery is under way: packets have been sent and the receiver is saying got it, watching for a gap.

concept: Damaged on the way? A checksum count that does not match means resend
alt: A later protocol level on the road: here a damaged packet must be spotted by its count and sent again.

concept: Two halves of security: physical protects the machine, digital the data
alt: Lock It in Pro opens with the sharing sort: security starts with knowing what must be protected.

concept: Physical or digital? Sort each measure by what it protects
alt: Physical or Digital: the sort whose bins are the machine and the data, from locked doors to firewalls.

concept: The padlock: details travel sealed, like an envelope, not a postcard
alt: The sealed route: a message travels a road marked sealed, the padlock idea played as a journey.

concept: Strong passphrases: four random words beat a short word plus a number
alt: The Pro mailbox key builder: a passphrase made of chosen words, different from every other account key.

concept: A shift of 3: every letter moves the same number of places
alt: The wheel at work: letters are shifting along the alphabet by the key, turning plain words into code.

concept: Brute force: a shift has only 25 keys, so you can try them all
alt: A later cipher level: with so few keys, trying every one is a real way in — for a shift cipher.

concept: Hiding is not scrambling: steganography hides a message in a picture's pixels
alt: Steganography: a heart hidden in a picture. Each pixel is a number, and its last bit says dot or blank, so the picture looks the same.

concept: Faked senders: a trick can fake its sender name, called spoofing
alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

concept: Write a credit line / share or keep: weigh both sides before sharing
alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.
